**Root cause:** Two-part variable name mismatch introduced when the parameter `device` was renamed to `device_filter`:

1. In `_run_wizard`: `ctx.invoke(scan, ..., device=None, ...)` — should be `device_filter=None`
2. In `scan`: `_scan_impl(..., device=device, ...)` — `device` is undefined, should be `device_filter`

This caused a `NameError` crash any time the wizard ran a scan or the `--device` filter was used.

**Fix:** Rename both callsites to `device_filter` to match the parameter definition.

**Testing:** Syntax verified; no behavioral change beyond the fix.

## Summary
Added `saveLocalSnapshot()` calls to ensure bean data modifications are persisted to local storage immediately after add, update, and delete operations.

## Key Changes
- **addBean()**: Call `saveLocalSnapshot()` after pushing new bean to `_beans` array
- **updateBean()**: Call `saveLocalSnapshot()` after updating bean in `_beans` array
- **deleteBean()**: Call `saveLocalSnapshot()` after removing bean from `_beans` array

## Implementation Details
These changes ensure that all mutations to the beans collection are immediately synchronized with local storage, preventing data loss and keeping the persisted state in sync with the in-memory state. Previously, local storage snapshots may have been saved only at specific intervals or user-triggered events, potentially leaving recent changes unsaved.

body:
**💡 What:** 
Optimized the `/bosses` endpoint in `backend/app/routes/arena.py` to eliminate N+1 queries. Modified the `get_boss_stats` function to accept `pre_count` and `pre_row` parameters, allowing the caller to pass in pre-computed values. Modified the query in `get_available_bosses` to batch fetch using `GROUP BY` instead of iteratively querying SQLite. Unused imports (`random`) were also cleaned up.

**🎯 Why:**
When fetching the list of available bosses, the application was executing an individual `SELECT COUNT(*)` query for every single subject, year, and custom boss, resulting in an O(N) database query explosion which bogged down the server.

**📊 Impact:**
Database queries drop from `O(N)` (e.g., ~100 queries if there are many subjects/years) down to just `O(1)` (3 queries total). This substantially speeds up the response time of the `/bosses` endpoint and reduces SQLite IO load.

**🔬 Measurement:**
This improvement can be verified by observing the request latency in the backend application logs when loading the Arena Bosses page on the frontend, or by intercepting the SQLite network/file IO. The endpoint will now respond consistently faster regardless of the number of bosses.

## Summary
This PR enhances the SST Navigator with three major UX improvements for self-represented litigants: grounded case summaries with source citations, an inline legal glossary for unfamiliar terms, and a balanced "legal landscape" view in fast mode that shows cases from different perspectives.

## Key Changes

### 1. Grounded Case Summaries with Source Citations
- Added `_GROUNDED_CASE_CARD_SYSTEM` prompt variant in `generator.py` that requires the model to attach paragraph references and confidence markers (explicit/inferred) to every factual claim
- Updated `generate_case_card()` method to accept a `grounded` parameter
- Implemented `_grounded_card_html()` function to render source citations with color-coded styling (green for explicit, orange for inferred)
- Modified UI to offer two generation buttons: "Generate summary" and "Generate grounded summary (with sources)"
- Added CSS styling for `.source-ref`, `.source-ref-explicit`, and `.source-ref-inferred` classes

### 2. Plain-Language Legal Glossary
- Created new `sst_navigator/glossary.py` module with 12 high-impact legal terms commonly found in SST decisions (e.g., "just cause," "severe and prolonged disability," "balance of probabilities")
- Each glossary entry includes plain-English definition and SST-specific context
- Implemented `detect_terms()` function using regex pattern matching to find glossary terms in text
- Added `_glossary_panel_html()` function to render detected terms as an inline panel below case cards
- Included comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_glossary.py`
- Added CSS styling for `.glossary-panel`, `.glossary-title`, `.glossary-term`, and related classes

### 3. Fast-Mode Legal Landscape Labeling
- Extended `SearchResult` dataclass with `landscape_role` field ("supportive", "unsupportive", "context", or empty)
- Added `landscape_mode` flag to `PipelineOutput` to indicate when results are labeled by perspective
- Implemented landscape pairing logic in `pipeline.py` that:
  - Selects one "supportive" case (Allowed outcome)
  - Selects one "unsupportive" case (Dismissed outcome)
  - Fills remaining slots with context/nuance cases
  - Ensures users see a balanced view of how courts have decided similar issues
- Implemented `_landscape_label_html()` function to render role badges with color-coded styling
- Added landscape notice banner explaining the balanced perspective approach
- Added CSS styling for `.landscape-label`, `.landscape-supportive`, `.landscape-unsupportive`, `.landscape-context`, and `.landscape-notice` classes

### 4. UI/UX Enhancements
- Added score interpretation legend (`_score_legend_html()`) explaining similarity score ranges (85%+, 70-84%, <70%)
- Landscape role labels appear above each result in fast mode
- Glossary panels render below both the top result and individual search results
- Two-column layout for generation buttons to accommodate both summary types
- Improved visual hierarchy with consistent color coding and typography

### 5. Supporting Changes
- Updated `pipeline.py` to pass `grounded` parameter through the generation pipeline
- Modified all generation backend methods (`_generate_mlx`, `_generate_openai`, `_generate_gemini`, `_generate_deepinfra`) to accept and forward the `grounded` parameter
- Added HTML escaping in glossary rendering to prevent injection vulnerabilities
- Implemented caching for both standard and grounded summaries with separate cache keys

## Implementation Details
- Glossary detection uses case-insensitive regex with word boundaries to avoid false matches
- Grounded summaries use paragraph number references (counted from document start) for traceability
- Fast-mode landscape pairing prioritizes outcome diversity while maintaining relevance ranking
- All new UI elements use consistent design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) matching existing components
- CSS uses gradient backgrounds and subtle borders for visual distinction without overwhelming the interface

## Summary

This PR improves how the bot responds to both user prompts and runtime failures.

It adds centralized in-channel error reporting with `ERROR_IMG`, updates truth-check responses to reply directly to the triggering message, and suppresses reply pings by default. It also tightens handler control flow so errors short-circuit cleanly without causing extra follow-up actions.

## Changes

- add shared error reporting for message handlers via `runMessageHandler()` and `reportMessageError()`
- send `ERROR_IMG` to the relevant channel when a handler fails while the bot is actively processing a message
- stop handler execution after an error so only one error image is sent per message flow
- preserve silent skipping for `messageUpdate` hydrate/fetch failures
- make Chinese-channel deletion errors bubble to the shared reporter instead of being swallowed locally
- prevent Chinese-channel delete failures from falling through into later handlers
- update truth-check handling to support `is it true that`
- change truth-check responses from `channel.send(...)` to `message.reply(...)`
- set global `allowedMentions.repliedUser: false` to avoid pinging the author on replies
- treat successful server renames and success reactions separately so a failed `✅` reaction does not look like a rename failure

## Why

These changes make bot failures visible in the same channel where the action was attempted, while avoiding false-positive error posts for messages the bot was not actually handling. They also make truth-check replies feel more directly attached to the triggering message without notifying the user unnecessarily.

## Testing

- verified syntax with `node --check index.js`
- live Discord behavior was manually checked, but cannot be verified due to human speeds

## Description

This has been going on for a while, and some trip over it more than others. I had been looking into it thinking it had something to do with `join_all`, which it didn't, but kept me down a similar path. I left a bunch of comments in the fix so people understand why it's there, but my running theory is that we `db_pool.close()` and immediately `drop_database()`, and Postgres isn't done cleaning up all of the backends yet, so it comes back saying other users are still accessing the database.

I could have changed it to a `DROP DATABASE WITH FORCE`, but figured it might be nicer to actually be gentle and check for active connections, and log while we wait.

Two things here are:
- If this does happen, it will be as intermittent as the flaky test is; it really shouldn't happen much.
- If this does happen, we won't see the logging unless we have `--nocapture` set.

I've never been able to get it to trip on my workstation, BUT, if we never see it flake again after this, then we know it was the fix. If the issue persists, then I'll rip it out.
